doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I’m fascinated that an artist of your standing would… I don’t know, and again, maybe it’s a risk-taking, but I’m wondering if it’s just a matter of keeping you intrigued, because to walk into a studio and put your career in the hands of something you don’t it’s gonna work.
Yeah.
Whereas, you could go in and play My Funny Valentine…
Yeah.
And How High the Moon and know that, you know, it would sell and be wonderful and whatever.
I hate that idea, though. You know me and…
Well, that’s what I…
Yeah.
Can you, can you talk a little bit in your voice about what it is that keeps you intrigued in moving and risk-taking?

Well, yeah, I thought I had kinda talked about that quite a bit. But I have a low boredom threshold, evidently, and that’s… since it is quote “an art form”… and I prefer Jackson Pollock to… (laughs) I told you about that scene I had with our friend.
Yes.

And it, it just… it’s a hammy word, but it’s just more interesting to me than playing… maybe it’s from all those years on the Merv Griffin Show, too. (laughs) I think I told you when I got out of the hospital, I didn’t have any money, and Gary Larson bought that guitar for me. It was very nice of him to do it. And I noticed when I was looking at it, right where the neck joins the… (laughs) the body, there was this whole big section where all the finish was worn off. I said, “How in the hell…” Then I realized I just spent hours sitting there with my hands folded over that part of the guitar and it wore all the finish off. (laughs)
Oh, wow.
Waiting for something interesting to happen… Then Ron bailed me out of that, I told you.
You mention occasionally not having any money.
Yes. (laughs)
And...
By the way, can I… I’m sorry. (laughs) How much do I get paid? Oh, I do get paid something.
Yes, you do get paid (for this?).
That’s right. I’d better shut up and talk.
Well, no, I’m, I’m curious about, again, about the… It keeps you interested, but you don’t know if it’s gonna pan out.
Yeah.
So that sort of takes me back to, I don’t know, faith and artistry, I guess.

Yeah. Well, that’s sort of like life itself, right? (laughs) You know, you’ll step out and get hit by a car maybe. (laughs) Or maybe you’ll have a heart attack, so you’d better do something interesting, anyway. (laughs)
Okay.
Yeah, I don’t mean to be…
